title: PluginWire
description:
Every structured value that crosses the plugin boundary, in one schema: the properties only
name the types, which are described under `$defs`. Which one a host function or an export
takes and returns is in the README of the plugin API; how a value is encoded is in its
"Wire format" section.

hostError.description: What every host function returns on failure, inside `{"status": "err", "data": …}`.

CachedFileDto.description: A verified file in the plugin's cache, returned by `download_to_cache`.

path.description:
Plugin-side path, readable through WASI: `/cache/downloads/<algorithm>/<hex digest>`.
The name is derived from the hash by the host, never from the plugin.

paths.description: The paths of the files, as `list_content` names them.

CommandRefusalDto.description: Why a command was not run.

oneOf.description: The user said no, or said it earlier and the plugin has not been reloaded since.
Nobody answered in time.
The plugin was stopped or removed.
The jar changed while the user was being asked.

ContentAuthorDto.description:
One item of the answer of `getAuthors`: who authors projects, by the `authorRef` of
`ContentMetadataDto`.

The answer, `GetAuthorsResultDto`, is a list of these, for the refs of
`GetAuthorsParamsDto`. A ref the provider does
not know is left out of the answer, not an error.

The host keeps only items whose `authorRef` was asked, once each, and with a non-blank
`name`; the rest of the answer is kept when one item is dropped. The name is trimmed and cut
to 128 characters.

name.description: The name to show as the author.

hash.description: Digest of the file: sha1 for files the app hashes itself, else whatever the pack recorded.

update.description:
Where the file can be updated from, one entry per provider.

A list rather than a map keyed by provider: a map key would need a string form of
[`ProviderIdDto`], which is two ids, not one string.

ContentIdentityDto.description:
One concrete file of a platform's content, in the ids of `ContentSourceDto::ProviderRef`, its
version always known.

iconUrl.description:
An `https` URL of the icon on a public host; empty when it has none. Any other value, or
one naming `localhost` or a private address, is dropped by the host.

url.description:
The content's page, an `http` or `https` URL; empty when it has none. Any other value is
dropped by the host.

ContentMetadataDto.description:
One item of the answer of `getContentsMetadata`: what the provider says about a project, to
show installed content by.

The answer, `GetContentsMetadataResultDto`, is a list of these, for the ids of
`GetContentsMetadataParamsDto`. An id the
provider does not know is left out of the answer, not an error.

The host keeps only items that answer an asked id by their `contentId` or by their `slug`
(compared without regard to case), and only the first of items with one `contentId`. An item
is kept under its `contentId`, so do not give an item the `slug` of one asked project and the
`contentId` of another. An item
without a `contentId` or a non-blank `name` is dropped; the rest of the answer is kept.

author.description: Absent when the provider cannot tell it without extra requests: the rest is shown alone.

authorRef.description:
The provider's own token for whoever authors the project (a team, an organization), when
naming them is a request apart: the host asks `getAuthors` for it later, so the project is
shown even when that request fails. Opaque to the host; used instead of `author` or
besides it. A blank ref, or one over 256 bytes, is no ref. The host also drops it when the
provider declares no `getAuthors`.

contentId.description:
The provider's own id of the project, which may differ from the one asked by (a slug, for
one).

iconUrl.description:
An `https` URL of the icon. The host downloads it itself, so the plugin needs no network
access to it; a URL of another scheme, with credentials, or naming `localhost` or an
address of a private network, is dropped.

slug.description:
The project's short name in URLs. Ids are also asked by it, so the host matches it to an
asked id.

page.description: The page the items are of, counted from 1 (the host refuses `0`, also for an empty result).

pageCount.description: How many pages the search has; `0` for no results.

pageSize.description: How many items a page holds, 1 to 1000 (the host refuses anything else).

ContentSourceDto.description: Where the bytes of a file come from.

oneOf.description:
An `https` URL to download, checked against the plugin's `allowedHosts` like its own
requests; any other refuses the plan. With a hash, the download is verified against it.

identity.description:
Which content of a platform the file is, when known (a pack listing a Modrinth CDN
URL). The file is then recorded with it for updates, and a new version of a mod the
user disabled stays disabled under a new file name.

oneOf.description:
Content hosted on a platform, resolved by the launcher through a provider serving that
platform (its `resolveFile`) — how a pack points at content it does not host, without
knowing which plugin serves it.

`platform` is the platform's name (`modrinth`, `curseforge`), not a plugin id;
`contentId` the platform's project id (Modrinth `AANobbMI`, `CurseForge` `238222`);
`version` the platform's id of one file of it (Modrinth version id, `CurseForge` file id),
absent — the newest file fitting the instance.

files.description:
The files of the version. A plugin built before it existed leaves it out and decodes with
an empty list.

webUrl.description:
The version's page, an `http` or `https` URL; empty when it has none. Any other value is
dropped by the host.

primary.description: The main file of the version.

ContentVersionMetadataDto.description:
One item of the answer of `getVersionsMetadata`: what the provider says about a version, to
show installed files by.

The answer, `GetVersionsMetadataResultDto`, is a list of these, for the ids of
`GetVersionsMetadataParamsDto`. An id the
provider does not know is left out of the answer, not an error.

The host keeps only items whose `versionId` was asked, once each, and with a non-blank
`versionNumber`; the rest of the answer is kept when one item is dropped.

name.description: The version's title, when the provider has one apart from its number.

versionId.description: The provider's own id of the version, as asked.

versionNumber.description: The version as its authors number it (`0.6.13+mc1.21.4`).

DownloadToCacheParamsDto.description:
Parameters of the `download_to_cache` host function.

The host downloads `url` into the plugin's `/cache`, verifies it against `hash` and only
then makes it visible. The network policy is the one of `http_get` (host `allowed_hosts`,
public addresses only, at most 5 redirects, each hop checked like the first request).

hash.description:
Expected digest of the file. Required: it is both the integrity check and the file's
name in the cache.

url.description: Absolute URL. Only the `http` and `https` schemes are accepted.

FileHashDto.description: An expected file digest, hex-encoded. Hex case does not matter.

FileSideDto.description: The side of the game a file is for.

GetAuthorsParamsDto.description: The input of `getAuthors`: the authors to name, asked in one go for a whole instance.

contentId.description: The provider's id of the project.

GetContentsMetadataParamsDto.description:
The input of `getContentsMetadata`: the projects to describe, asked in one go for a whole
instance.

contentIds.description: The provider's ids of the projects, or their slugs.

versionId.description: The provider's id of the version.

GetVersionsMetadataParamsDto.description:
The input of `getVersionsMetadata`: the versions to describe, asked in one go for a whole
instance.

versionIds.description: The provider's ids of the versions, as `ContentFileUpdateInfo::version` records them.

HashAlgorithmDto.description:
The algorithm of a [`FileHashDto`].

Md5 is deliberately not offered.

oneOf.description: 40 hex characters.
64 hex characters.
128 hex characters.

HttpPostJsonRequestDto.description:
A JSON POST request issued by a plugin through the `http_post_json` host function.

Same network policy as [`HttpRequestDto`] (host `allowed_hosts`, no non-public
addresses), except that redirects are never followed: any 3xx is an error. The host always
sends `Content-Type: application/json`.

body.description: Already-serialized JSON document. The host rejects a body that is not valid JSON.

url.description: Absolute URL. Only the `http` and `https` schemes are accepted.

HttpRequestDto.description:
A plain HTTP GET request issued by a plugin through the `http_get` host function.

Unlike Extism's built-in `http_request`, the host checks **every** redirect hop as if it
were the first request (`allowed_hosts`, public addresses, no `https` → `http`) and follows
at most 5 of them. The request headers are not sent on to another origin.

headers.description:
Extra request headers. Hop-by-hop and connection-control headers are rejected
by the host (see `HttpRequestDto` documentation in the plugin API README).

url.description: Absolute URL. Only the `http` and `https` schemes are accepted.

HttpResponseDto.description:
Response returned by the `http_get` and `http_post_json` host functions.

The body travels as a msgpack `bin`, not as an array of numbers: a plugin decodes it with a
copy instead of an instruction per byte, which is what keeps a megabyte-sized body within
the plugin's fuel.

body.description:
Response body. Truncation never happens silently: a body over the host limit
fails the whole call.

headers.description: Response headers, lowercased. Repeated headers are collapsed to the last value.

status.description: HTTP status code of the final response, after any redirects the host followed.

ImportSourceDto.description: What an importer reads an instance from: the input of `importInstance` names it.

oneOf.description: A file to download: an `http` or `https` address, already checked to be a valid one.
A file the plugin can read: a plugin-side path (`/mnt/<drive>/…` for a Windows path).

InstallFileEntryDto.description: One file the plan wants in the instance.

name.description:
What the file is called (a mod's or version's name), shown in the instance's content
list. Absent — the name `resolveFile` gives for a `providerRef`, or none.

relativePath.description:
Where the file goes, relative to the instance directory (`mods/sodium.jar`). `\` is
read as `/`. A path leaving the instance is refused when the file is written.

side.description: Absent — the file is for both sides.

size.description: Expected size in bytes, when known. Informational; the hash is what is verified.

InstallPlanDto.description: Everything a provider wants installed, and where.

files.description:
Every file the content needs, optional and server-side ones included: leaving files out
is the launcher's decision, made from the plan.

overrides.description: Applied in order, a later source's file replacing an earlier one's at the same path.

InstallTargetDto.description:
The instance a plan applies to.

Answers the request's `ResolveTargetDto`: `existing` with the same instance id, `new` with
the instance the content needs (a modpack's game version and loader). A plan for any other
instance is rejected.

game.description:
The game the instance runs once the plan is applied. Absent — the instance keeps its
game.

Only an update of the pack the instance was installed from may set it (its
`packInfo` names the provider and content the plan was resolved for); the request's
`gameVersion` and `loader` are then the instance's current state, not a requirement.
Any other plan with a game is rejected.

path.description: A path in the plugin's own file system (`/instances/…`).

InstanceFileBytesDto.description:
What `read_instance_file` returns: the file contents as a msgpack `bin`.

A newtype, so that the bytes can be encoded as `bin` — a bare `Vec<u8>` result would be an
array of numbers.

InstanceGameDto.description: What an instance runs, as a `NewInstanceDto` describes it.

loaderVersion.description:
Absent — not pinned: the instance keeps its loader version while the game version and
loader stay, and gets the default one otherwise.

InstanceIdParamsDto.description:
The input of the host functions that take one instance: `instance_get_dir`,
`instance_plugin_get_dir` and `list_content`.

InstanceSummaryDto.description:
What a plugin may learn about an instance it was not asked to work on: enough to judge
whether content fits it.

Deliberately without launch settings (`java_path`, `launch_args`, `env_vars`, `hooks`) and
host paths: users keep API keys and proxy credentials in the environment variables, and a
plugin with network access could send them out. Add a field here only when every plugin that
receives it needs it.

JavaDto.description: Description of a Java installation known to the launcher.

architecture.description: CPU architecture the installation was built for.

majorVersion.description: Major Java release number (for example 8, 17 or 21).

path.description: Filesystem location of the Java executable or installation.

version.description: Full version string reported by the installation.
The major Java release (for example 8, 17 or 21).

files.description: By the path of the file in the instance.

contentId.description: The provider's id of the project.

LogLevelDto.description: A log level, as the plugin names it.

ModLoaderDto.description:
Mod loader an instance can run on. Serialized as a lowercase string
(`vanilla`, `forge`, `fabric`, `quilt`, `neoforge`).

OptionalFileDto.description:
What makes a file optional: whether it is selected unless the user changes that, and what to
tell them about it.

OutputDto.description: Output of a command run through `run_command`. The streams travel as msgpack `bin`.

stderrTruncated.description: `stderr` hit the host's per-stream cap and was cut short.

stdoutTruncated.description: `stdout` hit the host's per-stream cap and was cut short.

OverrideLocationDto.description:
Where the files of an override source are.

Paths are plugin-side and must lie in the plugin's `/cache` (where `download_to_cache` puts
files); the launcher refuses anything else.

oneOf.description: The `subdir` directory of a zip archive (`overrides`).
A directory, copied recursively.

OverrideSourceDto.description:
Files copied into the instance as they are, on top of the planned ones (a modpack's
`overrides/`, `client-overrides/`).

side.description:
Absent — for both sides. As with files, a source for the other side stays in the plan:
the launcher leaves it out.

PackMetadataDto.description: The answer of `resolvePackMetadata`: a pack's description, read without resolving its files.

fileCount.description: How many files installing the pack would bring, when known without resolving them.

iconUrl.description: An `https` URL of the pack's icon on a public host; any other value is dropped by the host.

loaderVersion.description: Absent — the pack does not pin one.

versionId.description:
The platform's id of this version — what a check for updates compares. Absent when the
pack was not read from the platform and the provider cannot tell.

versionName.description: The version as the pack's author wrote it (`1.4.2`), for display only.

PackSourceDto.description: The input of `resolvePackMetadata`: where to read a pack from.

oneOf.description:
A pack hosted on the provider's platform; absent `version` — the version an update would
take from `installedVersion`, by the same rule as `ResolveInstallPlanParamsDto::version`,
which is how a check for updates asks.

installedVersion.description: The version of the pack the instance runs now.

oneOf.description: A pack file to download (a `.mrpack`, a packwiz `pack.toml`).
A pack file the plugin can read: a plugin-side path under `/cache` or `/instances`.

PluginCallErrorDto.description: Why a call into a plugin failed.

oneOf.description: The plugin reported that a command it asked for was not run, with the plugin's own words.
The user did not allow the plugin's command, or was not there to.

ReadInstanceFileParamsDto.description:
Parameters of the `read_instance_file` host function.

Same path rules as [`WriteInstanceFileParamsDto`].

relativePath.description: Path relative to the instance root, `/`-separated.

ResolveFileParamsDto.description: The input of `resolveFile`: which file a `providerRef` stands for.

loader.description:
The loader as written in `ResolveTargetDto::Existing` (`fabric`, `neoforge`); absent —
vanilla.

version.description:
Absent — the newest file that runs on `gameVersion` with `loader`. With a version, the
provider returns that file and need not check it against them.

ResolveInstallPlanParamsDto.description:
The input of `resolveInstallPlan`: which content to install, and into what. One shape for a
single mod and a whole modpack, for installing and updating alike.

installedVersion.description:
The platform's id of the version of this content installed in the target now; absent —
none is, or the launcher does not know it.

version.description:
Absent — the provider picks among the versions compatible with the target, by the
release channel: the newest release, or with `installedVersion` set, the newest version
of its channel (a beta takes betas and releases) that is newer than it — never an older
one; with nothing newer, the installed version itself.

ResolveTargetDto.description: Where the resolved plan is going to be applied; the plan's `InstallTargetDto` answers it.

oneOf.description:
Install into, or update, an existing instance, with the game version and loader it runs
now. For most content they are a requirement: it has to fit what the instance runs. For
the pack the instance was installed from (its `packInfo`) they are only the current
state: the plan of an update names the pack's game in `InstallTargetDto::Existing::game`,
and the launcher moves the instance to it.
A new instance, described by the content (a modpack).

ResolvedFileDto.description:
The answer of `resolveFile`: which bytes the ref stands for. No path: where the file goes is
the plan entry's `relativePath`.

fileName.description: The name the platform gives the file.

name.description: What the platform calls the file (a version's name), shown in the instance's content list.

url.description:
Downloaded under the same rules as a `direct` source of a plan: an `https` URL, or the
answer is refused.

version.description: The platform's id of the file the ref resolved to.

UpdateInstanceParamsDto.description: The input of an updater's export.

WriteInstanceFileParamsDto.description:
Parameters of the `write_instance_file` host function — the only way a plugin may put a
file inside an instance directory.

The path is **not** a WASI path: `/instances/<id>/...` and `/mnt/d/...` forms are refused.
A plugin names the instance by id and the file by a path relative to that instance's root,
and the host decides where that lands on disk.

bytes.description:
File contents. The whole file is replaced; the host caps the size. Travels as a msgpack
`bin` as the body of `HttpResponseDto` does.

instanceId.description: Id of an existing instance. An unknown id is an error, not a directory the host creates.

relativePath.description:
Path relative to the instance root, `/`-separated. Must be made of plain name segments:
no leading separator, no drive letter, no `.` or `..`.
